placements.role: Supplies UPS, switchgear, busbar and integrated power systems for hyperscale and colocation facilities.

role_evidence.claim: Vertiv's dated launch says PowerNexus combines Trinergy UPS with PowerBoard switchgear in a single block connected by internal busbars for data centers.

placements.role: Provides liquid-cooled thermal-management products and integrated cooling infrastructure for AI data centers.

role_evidence.claim: Vertiv's 2025 annual report lists liquid-cooled thermal-management products as part of its critical digital-infrastructure offering for AI applications.

business_summary: Vertiv Holdings Co is a NYSE-listed supplier of critical digital infrastructure: uninterruptible power supplies, switchgear, busbar, integrated power blocks and thermal management including liquid cooling, sold into hyperscale, colocation and enterprise data centres. Unlike the diversified industrials in this batch, its end market is the data centre itself, so its revenue line and the chain's demand are close to the same series.

exposure_summary.narrative: Vertiv sits on two links: power-equipment, the money corner, and liquid-cooling. Both placements are backed by dated product evidence, the PowerNexus launch for the power block and the 2025 Form 10-K for liquid-cooled thermal management. It is the most direct exposure in the batch and, for the same reason, the one where the un-crowded premise is weakest: an issuer whose entire business is the data centre is the first name a data-centre thesis reaches for.

implied_fcf_cagr.basis: Free-cash-flow CAGR the current enterprise value 98476100054.4 implies over a 5-year explicit period on base FCF 1893800000.0, solved by bisection on FCF CAGR at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. The discount rate and terminal growth are assumed, so the solve is an assumption-dependent expectation reading, not a reported figure.

horizon_spread.basis: Spread between the implied CAGR solved over the shortest and longest explicit periods in quality.reverse_dcf.implied_by_horizon ({'5': 0.3295, '7': 0.2438, '10': 0.1833}). It measures how much of the expectation reading is a horizon convention rather than a statement about price, and inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

data/market/VRT.json pcs records 26 analysts and 84.4% institutional ownership as of 2026-08-29, axis-B SATURATED, axis-A DARK at 88.2 under an ADVISORY gate.

disposition.basis: The most complete measurement set in the batch: every canonical field is sourced, Piotroski and Beneish both scored, and two filing-backed placements including the money corner. confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. INFERRED is a figure computed from SEC companyfacts, with the derivation named in its basis; where a market price enters the computation the basis says so explicitly, because the price leg is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/VRT.json, price_status AGREED) and not an issuer document. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.

capture.basis: The chain scores power-equipment capture at 72 on 'concentrated supply, long qualification, price escalators in backlog; genuine pricing power this cycle' (data/chains/ai-infrastructure.json). Vertiv's own operating margin of 17.89 percent for fiscal year 2025 (OperatingIncomeLoss 1829700000 over Revenues 10229900000, SEC companyfacts) sits below HUBBELL's 20.68 percent on the same link, consistent with a faster-growing, more competed data-center-facing sub-segment against Hubbell's utility-side product mix; both are equipment vendor economics, not the bid-competed contractor margin on grid-interconnect.
capture.what_would_change_it: Sustained margin expansion alongside the current growth rate would separate durable pricing power from capacity-driven volume; a margin roll-over on flat or rising revenue would be the earlier warning sign the profile's own crowdedness_caveats already flag on the valuation side.

quality.basis: Every canonical metric field resolves to a sourced number and none is NULL. Piotroski 6 (MIDDLING) and Beneish -2.438 (CLEAN) both compute from complete inputs. Net debt to EBITDA is 0.0604, effectively a net-cash balance sheet (total debt 2939800000 less cash 2810600000 as of 2026-06-30, over an EBITDA proxy of 2138300000 for fiscal year 2025). FCF margin of 18.51 percent and operating cash flow to net income of 1.586 are both the strongest in this pair and among the strongest in the theme.
quality.counterweight: MIDDLING, not STRONG, is the same Piotroski state as HUBBELL; the balance sheet and cash conversion are the standout, not the composite quality score.

expectations_gap.basis: The reverse DCF in data/market/VRT.json quality.reverse_dcf solves a 32.95 percent free-cash-flow CAGR over a five-year explicit period on base FCF 1893800000 at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth, against an achieved three-year revenue CAGR of 21.59 percent. Recorded plainly: this is the largest implied-versus-achieved gap of any profile in the batch, roughly 1.5 times achieved growth even before the horizon caveat. It is also exactly the tension the existing FINAL dive's own priced_in_summary already worked through at length (the 32.95 percent five-year solve read against a 14.62 to 37.52 percent horizon-sensitive band), which is why the dive closed WATCH rather than TOO_LATE or INVESTABLE. This dimension states the same measured gap fresh from current data; it does not re-adjudicate the verdict, which remains Stocky's and remains FINAL.
expectations_gap.horizon_caveat: The horizon spread is 14.62 percentage points (32.95 percent at five years against 18.33 percent at ten), the widest spread of any profile promoted this run. Per method section 7 a claimed gap smaller than that spread is a statement about horizon convention, not price.
expectations_gap.assumption_caveat: The discount rate and terminal growth are assumed, so both reverse-DCF fields are tagged SPECULATIVE. This dimension records the measured state only.

duplicate_exposure.basis: VERTIV-HOLDINGS holds two ACTIVE placements (liquid-cooling, power-equipment) and one listing. This same selection run also promotes HUBBELL on power-equipment, so the two O1 names share one link_id. Vertiv's role there is facility-side UPS, switchgear, busbar and integrated power blocks inside the data center; Hubbell's is utility-side and grid-facing transmission, substation and distribution equipment. Both are ACTIVE and filing-evidenced, and the sub-segments are economically distinct, but they share one demand cycle (data-center power buildout) and Stocky's independence test on either name should treat the other as correlated exposure, not a diversifying second bet.
